subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: After the safety findings and proof gap are resolved, should OpenClaw core accept a folder-backed encrypted snapshot backup flow with `backup.target` and `backup.encryption.key` config?
rationale: This adds new core CLI, config, SecretRef, and destructive restore behavior rather than a narrow bug fix, so maintainers need to confirm the product/API direction even if the implementation becomes correct.

options.title: Accept core direction after fixes
options.body: Keep this PR as the candidate for native encrypted folder snapshots once the safety findings, conflicts, and real proof are resolved.

options.title: Narrow to archive restore first
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR focused on local archive restore/export hardening while deferring folder-backed encrypted snapshots and workspace mirroring.

options.title: Defer to external tooling
options.body: Close or pause native snapshot work and continue recommending external/off-machine backup tools until core backup scope is settled.

recommendation.title: Accept core direction after fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as the candidate for native encrypted folder snapshots once the safety findings, conflicts, and real proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed/co-owned the original backup CLI and added adjacent backup-verify hardening, making them the strongest history-backed owner for the product/API choice among the inspected owners.
